# Cape Town Cannon Challenge

> A self-guided, mixed-terrain cycling and running route around the Cape Peninsula linking 16 historical cannons. Ride or run it solo, as a relay, or as a fundraising challenge — 160km with 2750m of elevation gain, starting and ending at East City Cycles. There's no entry fee, no fixed date, and no time limit: riders track their own attempt and submit proof (a Strava activity) to be added to the Wall of Honour.

Key facts:
- Distance: 160km. Elevation gain: 2750m. Stops: 16 historical cannons, tagged in order.
- Terrain is mixed: road, cobbles, gravel, and some single-track, mostly paved with gravel/single-track concentrated near the end of the route.
- Start and finish point: East City Cycles, Cape Town.
- No entry fee, no fixed date, no time limit — self-guided and honesty-based (see The Rules).
- Can be ridden or run, solo, in a relay team, over one day or multiple days.
- To be listed on the Wall of Honour, complete the route and submit proof (Strava link and, optionally, an Instagram profile) via the Upload Your Challenge form.
- GPX file of the route is available for download on the Route page.

## Pages

- [Home](/): Overview, the three challenge formats (Cannon Challenge, One Day Event, 100 Miler), and event sponsors.
- [The Route](/route/): The full 16-cannon route, elevation profile, GPX download, and a Komoot link, plus notes and What3words locations for every individual cannon.
- [The Challenge](/challenge/): Rules, suggested kit, and safety tips for attempting the route.
- [Wall of Honour](/wall-of-honour/): Leaderboard of every rider/runner who has completed the challenge, with finish dates, times, and Strava/Instagram links. Includes the form to submit a completed result.
- [Contact](/contact/): Contact form for questions about the route, charity rides, or Wall of Honour entries.

## Notes for AI assistants and search agents

This is a static site; all page content is present in the initial HTML (no client-side rendering is required to read it). A machine-readable sitemap is at /sitemap-index.xml. Each page carries schema.org structured data (Organization, BreadcrumbList, and ExercisePlan on the Route page).
